claim: Human mutations in the gene encoding the solute carrier (SLC) 6A17 caused intellectual disability (ID).
source: Human mutations in the gene encoding the solute carrier (SLC) 6A17 caused intellectual disability (ID).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature on human mutations in SLC6A17 causing ID.

claim: SLC6A17 protein was localized on synaptic vesicles (SVs).
source: Biochemistry, proteomic, and electron microscopy (EM) support SLC6A17 protein localization in synaptic vesicles (SVs).
evidence: The abstract states that biochemistry, proteomic, and EM approaches support this localization.

claim: Chemical analysis of SVs by liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (LC-MS) revealed glutamine (Gln) in SVs containing SLC6A17.
source: Chemical analysis of SVs by liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (LC-MS) revealed glutamine (Gln) in SVs containing SLC6A17.
evidence: The abstract describes LC-MS analysis that detected Gln in SVs with SLC6A17.

claim: Virally mediated overexpression of SLC6A17 increased Gln in SVs.
source: Virally mediated overexpression of SLC6A17 increased Gln in SVs.
evidence: The abstract states that viral overexpression of SLC6A17 increased Gln in SVs.

claim: Either genetic or virally mediated targeting of Slc6a17 reduced Gln in SVs.
source: Either genetic or virally mediated targeting of Slc6a17 reduced Gln in SVs.
evidence: The abstract states that both genetic and viral targeting of Slc6a17 reduced Gln in SVs.

claim: One ID mutation caused SLC6A17 mislocalization while the other caused defective Gln transport.
source: One ID mutation caused SLC6A17 mislocalization while the other caused defective Gln transport.
evidence: The abstract describes two different mechanisms by which ID mutations affect SLC6A17 function.

claim: SLC6A17 is necessary and sufficient for Gln transport into SVs.
source: Multidisciplinary approaches with seven types of genetically modified mice have shown Gln as an endogenous substrate of SLC6A17, uncovered Gln as a new molecule in SVs, established the necessary and sufficient roles of SLC6A17 in Gln transport into SVs
evidence: The abstract states that experiments with seven types of genetically modified mice established the necessary and sufficient roles of SLC6A17 in Gln transport.

claim: SV Gln decrease is the key pathogenetic mechanism in human ID caused by SLC6A17 mutations.
source: suggested SV Gln decrease as the key pathogenetic mechanism in human ID.
evidence: The abstract suggests that decreased Gln in SVs is the key mechanism underlying ID in patients with SLC6A17 mutations.

claim: Intellectual disability (ID) in humans has an approximate prevalence of 1%.
source: With an approximate prevalence of 1%, intellectual disability (ID) in humans is a neurodevelopmental disorder with debilitating effects on patients (Maulik et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Maulik et al., 2011.

claim: Mutations causing ID were found in the gene encoding SLC6A17.
source: Mutations causing ID were found in the gene encoding SLC6A17 (Iqbal et al., 2015; Waltl, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Iqbal et al., 2015 and Waltl, 2015.

claim: SLC6A17 was discovered 30 years ago.
source: SLC6A17, also known as Rxt1, NTT4, XT1, or B0AT3 (el Mestikawy et al., 1994; Liu et al., 1993), was discovered 30 years ago (el Mestikawy et al., 1994; Liu et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to el Mestikawy et al., 1994 and Liu et al., 1993.

claim: SLC6A17 is predominantly expressed in the nervous system.
source: It is predominantly expressed in the nervous system (el Mestikawy et al., 1994; Fischer et al., 1999; Hägglund et al., 2013; Jursky and Nelson, 1999; Kachidian et al., 1999; Luque et al., 1996; Masson et al., 1995; Masson et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: SLC6A17 protein was localized on synaptic vesicles (SVs) in previous studies.
source: SLC6A17 protein was localized on synaptic vesicles (SVs) (Fischer et al., 1999; Kachidian et al., 1999; Masson et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fischer et al., 1999; Kachidian et al., 1999; and Masson et al., 1999.

claim: Early efforts failed to identify substrates transported by SLC6A17.
source: Early efforts failed to identify substrates transported by SLC6A17 (Bröer, 2006; el Mestikawy et al., 1994; Liu et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bröer, 2006; el Mestikawy et al., 1994; and Liu et al., 1993.

claim: A study using PC12 cells and SLC6A17-transfected CHO cells found that SLC6A17 could transport four amino acids: proline (Pro), glycine (Gly), leucine (Leu), and alanine (Ala).
source: A later study using pheochromocytoma (PC)12 cells and SLC6A17-tranfected Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells found that SLC6A17 could transport four amino acids (AA): proline (Pro), glycine (Gly), leucine (Leu), and alanine (Ala) (Parra et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Parra et al., 2008.

claim: Another study using HEK cells reported transport of nine AAs: Leu, methionine (Met), Pro, cysteine (Cys), Ala, glutamine (Gln), serine (Ser), histidine (His), and Gly.
source: Another study using human embryonic kidney (HEK) cells reported transport of nine AAs: Leu, methionine (Met), Pro, cysteine (Cys), Ala, glutamine (Gln), serine (Ser), histidine (His), and Gly (Zaia and Reimer, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zaia and Reimer, 2009.

claim: None of the AAs reported as substrates of SLC6A17 in cell culture studies have been found in the SVs.
source: However, none of these AAs have been found in the SVs.
evidence: This statement is based on the absence of detection of these AAs in SVs in previous studies.

claim: Slc6a17 expression was found in the neocortex, the thalamus, the amygdala, the hippocampus, the pontine nuclei, and the brainstem.
source: Slc6a17 expression was found in the neocortex, the thalamus, the amygdala, the hippocampus, the pontine nuclei, and the brainstem (Figure 1B–K, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1 and supplementary figures.

claim: Strong expression of Slc6a17 was detected in the dentate gyrus (DG) and the CA3 region of the hippocampus.
source: Strong expression of Slc6a17 was detected in the dentate gyrus (DG) and the CA3 region of the hippocampus (Figure 1K), which is essential for spatial learning and memory.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Little expression of Slc6a17 was observed in either CA1 or CA2.
source: Little expression was observed in either CA1 or CA2 (Figure 1K).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Slc6a17 was also expressed in the basolateral amygdala (BLA).
source: Slc6a17 was also expressed in the basolateral amygdala (BLA) (Figure 1J), a brain area essential for emotion and fear learning.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Slc6a17-KO mice were not significantly different from the wild type (WT, Slc6a17+/+) mice in body weight.
source: These Slc6a17-KO mice were not significantly different from the wild type (WT, Slc6a17+/+) mice in body weight (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Slc6a17-KO mice were not significantly different from the wild type mice in basal activities.
source: These Slc6a17-KO mice were not significantly different from the wild type (WT, Slc6a17+/+) mice in body weight (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), basal activities (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Slc6a17-KO mice were not significantly different from the wild type mice in short-term memory.
source: These Slc6a17-KO mice were not significantly different from the wild type (WT, Slc6a17+/+) mice in body weight (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), basal activities (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), or short-term memory (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Slc6a17-/- mice exhibited a significant decrease in freezing behavior in both cued and contextual fear conditioning.
source: Slc6a17-/- mice exhibited a significant decrease in freezing behavior in both cued and contextual fear conditioning (day 2 context a, p=0.0062 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17-/-, p<0.0001 for Slc6a17+/- vs. Slc6a17-/-; Day 3 tone, p=0.0093 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17-/-, p=0.0012 for Slc6a17+/- vs. Slc6a17-/-).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2C with statistical analysis.

claim: Slc6a17-/- mice differed significantly from Slc6a17+/+ and Slc6a17+/- mice in latency to find the hidden platform during the training session of Morris water maze.
source: Slc6a17-/- mice differed significantly from Slc6a17+/+ and Slc6a17+/- mice (two-way ANOVA; main effect of training day: F (4.681, 210.7) = 46.55, p<0.0001; main effect of genotype: F (2, 45) = 21.53, p<0.0001; main effect of training day × genotype: F (12, 270) = 3.762, p<0.0001; Tukey's multiple comparisons test: day 2, p=0.0004 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17-/-, p=0.0002 for Slc6a17+/- vs. Slc6a17-/-; day 5, p=0.0002 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17-/-, p=0.008 for Slc6a17+/- vs. Slc6a17-/-; day 6, p=0.0002 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17-/-, p=0.0027 for Slc6a17+/- vs. Slc6a17-/-; day 7, p<0.0001 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17-/-, p=0.0005 for Slc6a17+/- vs. Slc6a17-/-).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2E with statistical analysis.

claim: Percentage of time spent in the target quadrant was significantly different between Slc6a17-/- mice and control mice in Morris water maze probe trial.
source: Percentage of time spent in the target quadrant was significantly different (p=0.0004 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17-/-, p<0.0001 for Slc6a17+/- vs. Slc6a17-/-).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2G with statistical analysis.

claim: Number of crossings through the platform area was significantly different between Slc6a17-/- mice and control mice in Morris water maze probe trial.
source: Number of crossings through the platform area was significantly different (p=0.0194 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17-/-, p=0.0054 for Slc6a17+/- vs. Slc6a17-/-).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2H with statistical analysis.

claim: Slc6a17-KO mice are significantly impaired both in contextual and cued fear memory and in hippocampus-dependent spatial learning and memory.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that Slc6a17-KO mice are significantly impaired both in contextual and cued fear memory and in hippocampus-dependent spatial learning and memory.
evidence: This statement is a summary of the behavioral data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Slc6a17P633R/P633R mutant mice were not significantly different from the WT or heterozygous in body weight.
source: Homozygous (Slc6a17P633R/P633R) mutant mice were not significantly different from the WT (Slc6a17+/+) or heterozygous (Slc6a17P633R/+) in body weight (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Slc6a17P633R/P633R mutant mice were not significantly different from the WT or heterozygous in basal activities.
source: Homozygous (Slc6a17P633R/P633R) mutant mice were not significantly different from the WT (Slc6a17+/+) or heterozygous (Slc6a17P633R/+) in body weight (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), basal activities (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Slc6a17P633R/P633R mutant mice were not significantly different from the WT or heterozygous in novel objection recognition.
source: Homozygous (Slc6a17P633R/P633R) mutant mice were not significantly different from the WT (Slc6a17+/+) or heterozygous (Slc6a17P633R/+) in body weight (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), basal activities (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), or novel objection recognition (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Slc6a17P633R homozygous mutants exhibited significant decrease of freezing behavior in both cued and contextual fear conditioning.
source: Slc6a17P633R homozygous mutants exhibited significant decrease of freezing behavior in both cued and contextual fear conditioning (day 2 context A, p<0.0001 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p<0.0001 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R; Day 3 tone, p=0.0017 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p=0.0009 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3D with statistical analysis.

claim: Slc6a17P633R/P633R mice showed significantly different learning curve from Slc6a17+/+ and Slc6a17P633R/+ mice in Morris water maze.
source: Slc6a17P633R/P633R mice showed significantly different learning curve from Slc6a17+/+ and Slc6a17P633R/+ mice (two-way ANOVA; main effect of training day: F (4.381, 144.6) = 20.02, p<0.0001; main effect of genotype: F (2, 33) = 22.65, p<0.0001; main effect of training day × genotype: F (12, 198) = 2.389, p=0.0067; Tukey's multiple-comparisons test: day 2, p=0.0150 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p=0.0078 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R; day 3, p=0.0403 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p=0.0388 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R; day 5, p=0.0023 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p=0.0243 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R; day 6, p=0.0199 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/+,p=0.0010 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p=0.0077 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R; day 7, p=0.0074 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p=0.0129 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3F with statistical analysis.

claim: Percentage of time spent in the target quadrant was significantly different between Slc6a17P633R/P633R mice and control mice in Morris water maze probe trial.
source: Percentage of time spent in the target quadrant was significantly different (p=0.0031 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p=0.0325 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3H with statistical analysis.

claim: Number of crossings through the platform area was significantly different between Slc6a17P633R/P633R mice and control mice in Morris water maze probe trial.
source: Number of crossings through the platform area was significantly different (p=0.0003 for Slc6a17+/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R, p=0.0123 for Slc6a17P633R/+ vs. Slc6a17P633R/P633R).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3I with statistical analysis.

claim: Slc6a17P633R mice are significantly impaired both in contextual and cued fear memory and in hippocampus-dependent long-term spatial learning.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that Slc6a17P633R mice are also significantly impaired both in contextual and cued fear memory and in hippocampus-dependent long-term spatial learning.
evidence: This statement is a summary of the behavioral data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The point mutation P633R is a LOF mutation.
source: Because all the phenotypes of Slc6a17P633R are similar to Slc6a7-KO, the point mutation P633R is a LOF mutation.
evidence: This statement is based on the similarity of phenotypes between Slc6a17P633R and Slc6a17-KO mice.

claim: SLC6A17-HA was enriched in LP2 fraction, similar to other SV proteins.
source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, SLC6A17-HA was enriched in LP2 fraction, similar to the other SV proteins such as synaptotagmin 1 (Syt1) (Geppert et al., 1994), vesicular ATPase (V-ATPase) (Cidon and Sihra, 1989), and synaptobrevin 2 (Syb2) (Link et al., 1992; Schiavo et al., 1992), but different from postsynaptic proteins such as postsynaptic density 95 (PSD95) (Cho et al., 1992; Woods and Bryant, 1991).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and citations to published literature.

claim: Sucrose gradient centrifugation of the LP2 fraction showed copurification of SLC6A17-HA with SV proteins.
source: Sucrose gradient centrifugation of the LP2 fraction showed copurification of SLC6A17-HA with SV proteins including synaptophysin (Syp) (Jahn et al., 1985; Leube et al., 1987; Wiedenmann and Franke, 1985), Syt1, and VGluT1 (Bellocchio et al., 2000; Takamori et al., 2000), but not with proteins localized to the postsynaptic membrane (PSD95) or (SNAP23) (Ravichandran et al., 1996; Suh et al., 2010), the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (ERp72), the endosome (EEA1) (Mu et al., 1995), and the proteosome (PSMC6) or the trans-Golgi network (synaptaxin 6, STX6) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4D and citations to published literature.

claim: The fraction containing SLC6A17-HA was found to be co-localized with SV markers.
source: After examining markers of subcellular organelles, the fraction containing SLC6A17-HA was found to be co-localized with SV markers such as Syp, Syt1, Syb2, VATPase, and vesicular neurotransmitter transporters including VGluT1, VGluT2, and VGAT (Figure 4C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The fraction containing SLC6A17-HA was not co-localized with markers of various non-SV organelles.
source: but not with markers of axons or dendrites (GLUT4 or transferrin receptor), ER (ERp72), the lysosome (LAMP2, LC3b, or cathepsin D), the cytoplasmic membrane (SNAP23, PSD95, and GluN1), the Golgi apparatus (GM130 and Goglin-97), mitochondria (VADC), the active zone (ERC1b/2), the endosome (EEA1), and the proteosome (PSMC6) (Figure 4C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Immunostaining of HA-tagged SLC6A17 in Slc6a17HA/+ mouse showed puncta co-localized with the anti-Syp positive immunoreactivity.
source: In addition, immunostaining of HA-tagged SLC6A17 in Slc6a17HA/+ mouse showed puncta co-localized with the anti-Syp positive immunoreactivity (Figure 4B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: SLC6A17-APEX2 was indeed localized on the SVs.
source: SLC6A17-APEX2 was indeed localized on the SVs (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, C, E, and G).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Quantitative analysis showed distinct populations of SVs distinguished by electron density.
source: Quantitative analysis showed distinct populations of SVs distinguished by electron density (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, D, F, and H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: SLC6A17 was the only transporter significantly decreased in Slc6a17-KO mice.
source: Quantitative proteomic analysis showed that only SLC6A17 was dramatically reduced in SVs immunopurified from Slc6a17-KO mice, whereas other transporters such as VGluT1, VGluT2, VGluT3, VGAT, VMAT2, SV2A, SV2B, SV2C, ZnT3, and VAT-1 were not different between Slc6a17-/- and Slc6a17+/+ (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: SLC6A17P633R-HA signal was primarily localized to the soma with no overlap detected with the anti-Syp antibody staining.
source: With the endogenous SLC6A17P633R protein tagged by the HA and FLAG epitopes (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), we found that SLC6A17P633R-HA signal was primarily localized to the soma with no overlap detected with the anti-Syp antibody staining (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: HA and FLAG signals were presented in LP2 but did not co-purified with SVs in sucrose gradients, indicated that the SLC6A17P633R protein was not present in SVs.
source: We also performed differential centrifugation and sucrose gradient purification. HA and FLAG signals were presented in LP2 but did not co-purified with SVs in sucrose gradients, indicated that the SLC6A17P633R protein was not present in SVs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Glu, GABA, and ACh were reliably detected from SVs immunoisolated with the anti-Syp antibody.
source: Glu, GABA, and ACh were reliably detected from SVs immunoisolated with the anti-Syp antibody (Figure 5C–G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, D, and F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Of the nine AAs reported previously using cultured cells, eight (Ala, Gly, Leu, Pro, Cys, Gly, His, and Ser) were not found to be significantly enriched in SVs.
source: Surprisingly, of the nine AAs reported previously using cultured cells, eight (Ala, Gly, Leu, Pro, Cys, Gly, His, and Ser) were not found to be significantly enriched in SVs (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Only Gln was reproducibly found to be enriched in the anti-Syp antibody immunoisolated SVs.
source: Only Gln was reproducibly found to be enriched in the anti-Syp antibody immunoisolated SVs (Figure 5C, D and H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5C, D, and H.

claim: Significant enrichment of Gln was detected in SVs containing SLC6A17-HA.
source: Significant enrichment of Gln was detected in SVs containing SLC6A17-HA (Figure 6C, D, and H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6C, D, and H.

claim: The other eight AAs had not been found to be enriched in SVs containing SLC6A17-HA.
source: By contrast, the other eight AAs had not been found to be enriched in SVs containing SLC6A17-HA (Figure 6C, D, and I).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6C, D, and I.

claim: The overexpressed SLC6A17-HA protein was localized in SVs.
source: The overexpressed SLC6A17-HA protein was localized in SVs, as analyzed by immunoblot (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SVs from mice overexpressing SLC6A17-HA contained significantly higher levels of Glu and GABA.
source: SVs from mice overexpressing SLC6A17-HA contained significantly higher levels of Glu and GABA (Figure 7B–G).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7B-G.

claim: Gln was dramatically increased in SVs overexpressing SLC6A17-HA.
source: Gln was dramatically increased (Figure 7B and F), to the extent that Gln was higher than GABA in SVs overexpressing SLC6A17-HA (Figure 7B, D, F, K, and M).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7B, F, K, and M.

claim: Quantification of the enriched molecules in SVs containing SLC6A17-HA showed Gln to be approximately two times that of GABA.
source: Quantification of the enriched molecules in SVs containing SLC6A17-HA showed Gln to be approximately two times that of GABA (Figure 7D and F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7D and F.

claim: His was moderately increased in SVs overexpressing SLC6A17-HA.
source: In addition, His was moderately increased in SVs overexpressing SLC6A17-HA (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: Overexpressed SLC6A17G162R-HA was still localized on SVs.
source: Overexpressed SLC6A17G162R-HA was still localized on SVs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and E.

claim: Levels of Glu and GABA in SVs containing SLC6A17G162R-HA were higher than those in WT mice.
source: Levels of Glu and GABA in SVs containing SLC6A17G162R-HA were higher than those in WT mice (Figure 7J and K, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), but not significantly different with those from OE-Syp-HA mice (Figure 7J and K).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7J, K, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The level of Gln in SVs containing SLC6A17G162R-HA were much lower than that in from OE-SLC6A17-HA mice.
source: The level of Gln in SVs containing SLC6A17G162R-HA were much lower than that in from OE-SLC6A17-HA mice (Figure 7M), indicating that SLC6A17G162R was defective in transporting Gln into SVs in vivo.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7M.

claim: SLC6A17G162R was defective in transporting Gln into SVs in vivo.
source: The level of Gln in SVs containing SLC6A17G162R-HA were much lower than that in from OE-SLC6A17-HA mice (Figure 7M), indicating that SLC6A17G162R was defective in transporting Gln into SVs in vivo.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the data shown in Figure 7M.

claim: The level of Gln in SVs containing SLC6A17G162R-HA was higher than that in WT mice, but not different from that in OE-Syp-HA mice.
source: The level of Gln in SVs containing SLC6A17G162R-HA was higher than that in WT mice, but not different from that in OE-Syp-HA mice (Figure 7M).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7M.

claim: Gln was increased most dramatically in SVs overexpressing SLC6A17-HA, compared to those overexpressing Syp-HA or SLC6A17G162R-HA.
source: Gln was increased most dramatically in SVs overexpressing SLC6A17-HA, compared to those overexpressing Syp-HA (Figure 7I and M) or SLC6A17G162R-HA (Figure 7H and M).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7H, I, and M.

claim: Gln was the only molecule found to be decreased in SVs from Slc6a17-/- mice, compared with Slc6a17+/+ or Slc6a17+/- mice.
source: LC-MS analysis of SVs revealed that Gln was the only molecule found to be decreased in SVs from Slc6a17-/- mice, compared with Slc6a17+/+ or Slc6a17+/- mice (Figure 8H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8H.

claim: The levels of classic transmitters such as Glu, GABA, and ACh were not significantly different among the SVs immunoisolated from the Slc6a17+/+, the Slc6a17+/-, or the Slc6a17-/- mice.
source: Quantitative analysis showed that the levels of classic transmitters such as Glu (Figure 8A), GABA (Figure 8B), and ACh (Figure 8C) were not significantly different among the SVs immunoisolated from the Slc6a17+/+, the Slc6a17+/-, or the Slc6a17-/- mice.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8A, B, and C.

claim: The levels of the other eight AAs were also not significantly different among SVs immunoisolated from all three genotypes.
source: The levels of the other eight AAs were also not significantly different among SVs immunoisolated from all three genotypes (Figure 8D–F, G, I– L).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8D-L.

claim: Slc6a17-HA was significantly reduced both in the homogenates of total brains and in immunoisolated SVs from AAV-sgRNA/Slc6a17iCre/Cas9+ mice.
source: Slc6a17-HA was significantly reduced both in the homogenates of total brains and in immunoisolated SVs from AAV-sgRNA/Slc6a17iCre/Cas9+ mice (Figure 9B, Figure 9—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9B and Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Gln was the only vesicular content significantly decreased in SVs from the knockout mice.
source: Importantly, when the SV contents from the brains of knockout (AAV-sgRNA/Slc6a17iCre/Cas9+) and control (AAV-sgRNA/Slc6a17iCre/Cas9-) mice were compared after LC-MS analysis, Gln was the only vesicular content significantly decreased in SVs from the knockout mice (Figure 9C, D, and H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9C, D, and H.

claim: GABA and Glu were moderately increased in SVs from adult Slc6a17 knockout mice.
source: To our surprise, GABA and Glu were moderately increased (Figure 9C–F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9C-F.

claim: The level of ACh, and those of the other eight AAs (Ala, Gly, Leu, Pro, Cys, Gly, His, and Ser), was not significantly changed in the SVs from adult Slc6a17 knockout mice.
source: The level of ACh, and those of the other eight AAs (Ala, Gly, Leu, Pro, Cys, Gly, His, and Ser), was not significantly changed in the SVs from adult Slc6a17 knockout mice (Figure 9C, D, G, and I).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9C, D, G, and I.

claim: SLC6A17 is physiologically necessary for Gln in SVs, but not for the other eight AAs.
source: These results indicate that SLC6A17 is physiologically necessary for Gln in SVs, but not for the other eight AAs.
evidence: This statement is a summary of the data from the virally mediated knockout experiment.

claim: Gln transport into the SVs was decreased in Slc6a17P633R mutant mice.
source: Gln transport into the SVs was decreased in Slc6a17P633R mutant mice (Figure 10I).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 10H.

claim: A significant decrease in Gln level in Slc6a17P633R/P633R, compared to Slc6a17+/+ and Slc6a17P633R/+ mice.
source: LC-MS analysis of contents from SVs showed a significant decrease in Gln level in Slc6a17P633R/P633R, compared to Slc6a17+/+ and Slc6a17P633R/+ mice (Figure 10H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 10H.

claim: The levels of Glu, GABA, and ACh in SVs were not significantly different among Slc6a17+/+, Slc6a17P633R/+, and Slc6a17P633R/P633R mice.
source: The levels of Glu (Figure 10A), GABA (Figure 10B), and ACh (Figure 10C) in SVs were not significantly different among Slc6a17+/+, Slc6a17P633R/+, and Slc6a17P633R/P633R mice.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 10A, B, and C.

claim: The levels of the other eight AAs in the SVs were also not significantly different among Slc6a17+/+, Slc6a17P633R/+, and Slc6a17P633R/P633R mice.
source: The levels of the other eight AAs in the SVs were also not significantly different among Slc6a17+/+, Slc6a17P633R/+, and Slc6a17P633R/P633R mice (Figure 10D–G, I–L).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 10D-L.

claim: Mislocalization of SLC6A17P633R outside the SVs correlates with the inability of Gln enrichment in SVs.
source: Thus, mislocalization of SLC6A17P633R outside the SVs correlates with the inability of Gln enrichment in SVs (Figure 10H), as well as behavioral impairment (Figure 3D, F, H, and I), establishing the significance of SLC6A17 localization on the SVs.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the correlation between mislocalization and Gln reduction.

claim: Two mutations pathogenic for human ID both resulted in reduction of Gln in the SVs.
source: We have discovered the presence of Gln in the SVs and shown that it is functionally important because two mutations pathogenic for human ID patients both resulted in reduction of Gln in the SVs.
evidence: This statement is a summary of the findings from the two point mutation studies.

claim: The human ID mutation Slc6a17P633R causes mislocalization of SLC6A17 outside the SVs.
source: We demonstrate the functional significance of the SV localization of SLC6A17 by showing that the human ID mutation Slc6a17P633R causes mislocalization of SLC6A17 outside the SVs (Figure 3B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: SLC6A17 is sufficient for Gln presence in SVs.
source: With multiple rounds of biochemical purification of SVs and chemical analysis of SV contents of genetically modified mice, we have found that Gln is present in SVs containing SLC6A17 and that SLC6A17 is sufficient for Gln presence in SVs (Figures 5—7).
evidence: This statement is a summary of the findings from the overexpression experiments.

claim: Gln is the only molecule reliably and reproducibly reduced in SVs when Slc6a17 gene is deleted.
source: With two lines of germline mutant mice and virally mediated gene edited mice, we demonstrate that Gln is the only molecule reliably and reproducibly reduced in SVs when Slc6a17 gene is deleted (Figures 8 and 9).
evidence: This statement is a summary of the findings from the knockout experiments.

claim: SLC6A17G162R could not transport Gln into SVs.
source: We have also characterized mice carrying a human ID mutation SLC6A17G162R and found it could not transport Gln into SVs (Figure 7), further supporting the importance of Gln in SVs.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Two mutations pathogenic in human ID are both LOF mutations: SLC6A17P633R with mislocalization outside the SVs and the SLC6A17G162R with defective Gln transport into the SVs.
source: Thus, two mutations pathogenic in human ID are both LOF mutations: SLC6A17P633R with mislocalization outside the SVs and the SLC6A17G162R with defective Gln transport into the SVs.
evidence: This statement is a summary of the findings from the two point mutation studies.

claim: All four kinds of SLC6A17 LOF mutations (two KOs, two point mutations) have led to reduction in Gln in SVs.
source: The fact that all four kinds of SLC6A17 LOF mutations (two KOs, two point mutations) have led to reduction in Gln in SVs strongly support the functional significance of Gln in SVs.
evidence: This statement is a summary of the findings from all the genetic manipulation experiments.

claim: SLC6A17 is a member of the SLC6 family, which is also known as the NTT family because many members of this family are transporters for neurotransmitters.
source: SLC6A17 is a member of the SLC6 family, which is also known as the NTT family because many members of this family are transporters for neurotransmitters (Blakely and Edwards, 2012; Bröer, 2006; Kristensen et al., 2011; Rudnick et al., 2014)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: There is a Glu/Gln cycle in which Glu released from neurons is taken up by glia and transformed into Gln, followed by Gln release from glia and taken up by neurons and transformed into Glu.
source: There is a Glu/Gln cycle in which Glu released from neurons is taken up by glia and transformed into Gln, followed by Gln release from glia and taken up by neurons and transformed into Glu (Bak et al., 2006; Benjamin and Quastel, 1972; Ottersen et al., 1992; van den Berg and Garfinkel, 1971).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: It is unlikely that SLC6A17 and the Gln transports could be part of the Glu/Gln cycle.
source: It is unlikely that SLC6A17 and the Gln transports could be part of the Glu/Gln cycle because (1) the Glu/Gln cycle uses cytoplasmic transporters for Gln, not vesicular transporters for Gln; (2) Gln is transformed into Glu in the cytoplasm of neurons before being transported in the SVs as Glu; and (3) in all of our experiments presented here, when SLC6A17 was genetically disrupted, Gln was consistently decreased, but Glu was either unchanged but not concomitantly increased, which was against the expectation of the Glu/Gln cycle.
evidence: This statement is based on logical inference from the data and knowledge of the Glu/Gln cycle.

claim: Gln is one of the major carbon sources.
source: The possibility of Gln as a carbon source is based on the fact that it is one of the major carbon sources (Hensley et al., 2013; Reitzer et al., 1979).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.
